findings: Gateway namespace absence is required before Sandbox deletion. This prevents the Gateway from creating more Sandbox work during cleanup.
Both state namespaces require completed SQL and workload observations before deletion.
The generated allocator removes owned cluster bindings before it requests namespace deletion. A false completion result does not prove that namespace deletion has been requested.
DeleteOwned verifies ownership and object identity. It uses UID and resource-version preconditions with foreground deletion and waits for absence. It does not remove finalizers.
The allocation controller already requests a one-second pending recheck. The workload controller still uses the error-returning runner at this source.
Namespace observations record conditions and read-return times. They do not identify the cause of every delay.
decision: Keep all namespace dependency barriers, finalizers, and grace periods. Test the workload adapter with the existing common pending-result API. Do not claim a latency cause or a target pass.
